uncited: This method provides interactive, selective suppression of volume data using two complementary geometric primitives: an axis-aligned **Clipping Cube** and an arbitrary **Cutting Plane**.
It solves the problem of isolating specific anatomical or structural regions (focus) while maintaining spatial context of the surrounding volume.
**Clipping Cube Widget:** Represented as a wireframe cube with eight spheres at its corners.
**Cutting Plane:** Defined by a normal vector and a distance from the origin, or by two points in space.
*   **Clipping Mode:** Determines the behavior of the volume outside the clipping cube.
**Initialize Clipping Cube:** The system renders a wireframe cube with spheres at the corners.
*   The user moves the pen into the vicinity of a corner sphere.
The cube resizes non-uniformly, maintaining its axis-aligned orientation.
*   The PIP pad itself acts as the cutting plane.
*   The user presses the **second pen button** to freeze the plane in place.
This variant specifically utilizes Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR) for the context region.
It isolates a focus region using a clipping cube widget (rendered as a surface) while rendering the context outside the cube as non-photorealistic contours.
This approach is chosen when the user needs to see the structural outline of the clipped volume without the visual clutter of full volume rendering.
The clipping cube widget is resizable via corner dragging and defines the bounded region for clipping.
*   **Time Complexity:** Rendering time depends on the volume rendering algorithm (e.g., ray casting).
The clipping operation itself is $O(1)$ per pixel as it is handled by hardware-accelerated OpenGL clipping planes.
*   **Memory Complexity:** The clipping cube and cutting plane data structures are constant size ($O(1)$).
The focus-plus-context approach with NPR provides clear structural context.
*   **When to use:** When exploring internal structures of a volume while needing to see the surrounding context's shape.
This method was developed for distributed software-based volume visualization in a virtual environment.
It builds on earlier work in focus-plus-context visualization [FG98] and integrates with existing RTVR (Real-Time Volume Rendering) capabilities for axis-aligned and oblique clipping.
